mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real GDP signals a weakening economy, reducing consumer and business spending, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances following a 3-month GDP decline, or GDP decline does not precede a significant downturn in S&P 500 returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals labor market weakness, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 2% within the last month signals supply chain disruptions and reduced output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts signals a strengthening economy and increased consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances following a sustained increase in housing starts, or the increase in housing starts does not precede a significant uptick in S&P 500 returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and CPI inflation is rising, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3% within the last month, the combination signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect of strong PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is positive and retail sales are increasing, the combination signals a robust consumer demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth positive and RSAFS increasing
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect of positive GDPC1 growth and increasing RSAFS on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
